vep_command: vep -i variants.vcf -o <out> --offline --cache --dir_cache <cache> --cache_version 116 --species homo_sapiens --assembly GRCh38 --format vcf --buffer_size 5000 --fork 1 --fasta reference.fa --no_stats --quiet --force_overwrite [--tab|--vcf|--json]
input: 25 hand-built records on chromosome 21 and MT as a VCF (variants.vcf): on KRTAP24-1 a stop-lost SNV written five ways (the plain notation, a lower-case alternate, the NC_000021.9 accession, the chr21 spelling and a (p.=) suffix), a missense and a synonymous SNV, an in-frame three-base deletion, a one-base frameshift deletion, a one-base frameshift insertion, a twenty-base deletion, a three-base delins and a three-base inversion of the same codon, a delins trimmed to the SNV and a one-for-two delins; on KRTAP25-1 a one-base duplication written as dup and as an insertion with its positions reversed; the stop-retained deletion on KRTAP26-1; the stop-lost deletion on KRTAP23-1, twice (its notation lists the deleted bases rightly and then wrongly); the five-base duplication and insertion on KRTAP13-4; the MT-ATP6 missense and the MT-TL1 tRNA SNV; an intergenic SNV; and, record for record in the same order, the same variants as HGVS genomic notation (variants.hgvs.txt), each a g. or m. shape Ensembl VEP resolves through its database

hgvs.perl_cache: none: the transcripts, the slice sequence and the HGVS resolution come from the database
hgvs.fasta: none on the Ensembl VEP side (the slice sequence comes from the database); reference.fa.gz on the vep-rs side
hgvs.vep_command: vep -i variants.hgvs.txt -o <out> --database --host useastdb.ensembl.org --port 3306 --user anonymous --db_version 116 --species homo_sapiens --assembly GRCh38 --format hgvs --buffer_size 5000 --fork 1 --no_stats --force_overwrite [--tab|--vcf|--json]
hgvs.database_snapshot: Ensembl release 116 (db_version 116): the release databases are fixed snapshots, so the run reads the same transcripts and sequence whenever it is repeated

hgvs-guess.perl_cache: none: the transcripts, the slice sequence and the HGVS resolution come from the database
hgvs-guess.fasta: none on the Ensembl VEP side (the slice sequence comes from the database); reference.fa.gz on the vep-rs side
hgvs-guess.vep_command: vep -i variants.hgvs.txt -o <out> --database --host useastdb.ensembl.org --port 3306 --user anonymous --db_version 116 --species homo_sapiens --assembly GRCh38 --buffer_size 5000 --fork 1 --no_stats --force_overwrite [--tab|--vcf|--json]
hgvs-guess.expected_outputs: the hgvs set's files (expected_hgvs): Ensembl VEP detects the format from the first data line, so its output for the input without --format is the output of the hgvs set
hgvs-guess.database_snapshot: Ensembl release 116 (db_version 116): the release databases are fixed snapshots, so the run reads the same transcripts and sequence whenever it is repeated

generator: variants.vcf and manifest.json by scripts/golden/build_golden_corpus.py select over Ensembl VEP's default output for the VCF; expected/ by scripts/concordance/generate_reference_output.sh --corpus; expected_hgvs/ by one container run per format of the same image in database mode (--database --db_version 116, no cache, no FASTA) on variants.hgvs.txt, the four outputs gzipped and their sha256 recorded under flag_sets; json_cache by scripts/golden/prune_json_cache.py over the release-116 GRCh38 cache (--drop sorted_exons --drop protein_features --drop protein_function_predictions); reference.fa.gz is GRCh38 chromosome 21 with every base outside 2,000 bases of a record masked to N, and MT whole, bgzip-compressed with reference.fa.gz.fai and reference.fa.gz.gzi for the compressed file and reference.fa.fai for its decompressed form
